episodes.title: Yellow Cake
episodes.description: Martha demonstrates the fundamentals of American yellow cake, starting with her father's favorite birthday cake layered with orange curd and finished with chocolate frosting. She also prepares upside-down cakes with stone fruit and feather-light strawberry cupcakes, explaining how butter temperature affects crumb structure.
recipes: Yellow Birthday Cake with Chocolate Frosting

episodes.title: Pâte Brisée
episodes.description: Martha walks through her master shortcrust pastry from scratch, demonstrating how fat temperature and minimal handling produce flaky results. She uses the dough to make a towering mile-high apple pie, poached pears wrapped in golden pastry, and a savory tomato tart with fresh herbs.

episodes.title: Cheesecake
episodes.description: A master class in American-style cheesecake, covering the classic New York version baked in a water bath for a silky, crack-free finish. Martha also makes an Italian ricotta cheesecake scented with orange peel and petite individual cherry cheesecakes perfect for entertaining.

episodes.title: Pound Cake
episodes.description: Martha explores the pound cake tradition, tracing its origins to the old rule of a pound each of butter, flour, eggs, and sugar. She bakes a bright Meyer lemon version and a cream cheese variation that stays moist for days, explaining why the high-fat batter needs gentle folding.

episodes.title: Muffins and Popovers
episodes.description: Two quick-rise favorites in one episode. Martha's blueberry muffins highlight the importance of not over-mixing, keeping the batter lumpy for a tender crumb. Her classic popovers rely on steam rather than leavening to create their dramatic hollow interior.

episodes.title: Puff Pastry
episodes.description: Martha demystifies classic pâte à choux, the simple four-ingredient cooked dough behind French pastry staples. She pipes and bakes cream puffs, éclairs finished with chocolate glaze, golden profiteroles, and savory gougères flavored with Gruyère cheese.

episodes.title: Meringues
episodes.description: Martha covers all three meringue styles — French, Swiss, and Italian — through three dramatic desserts. A passion fruit pavlova showcases French meringue's crisp exterior and marshmallow center; île flottante brings poached Swiss meringue islands floating in crème anglaise; and a Southern Huguenot torte rounds out the lesson.

episodes.title: Pâte Sucrée
episodes.description: Martha makes her sweet tart dough from scratch, pressing it into fluted tart pans and blind-baking to a golden shell. She fills the shells with silky lemon curd, then prepares a dark chocolate ganache tart that sets to a clean, glossy slice.

episodes.title: Yeast Breads
episodes.description: A primer on working with yeast: how to proof, how to judge a properly developed dough, and how to shape. Martha bakes fluffy dinner rolls, sticky cinnamon buns with cream cheese icing, and dimpled focaccia dressed with rosemary and sea salt.
recipes: Cinnamon Buns with Cream Cheese Icing

episodes.title: Devil's Food Cake
episodes.description: Martha explores chocolate's role in layer cakes, explaining the chemical difference between natural cocoa and Dutch-process and how each affects color and flavor. She bakes a deep, moist devil's food layer cake with billowy frosting and a lavish chocolate mousse cake.

episodes.title: Cookies
episodes.description: Martha covers the major American cookie categories: drop, rolled, and pressed. She bakes the definitive chocolate chip cookie with brown butter for depth, elegant linzer sandwich cookies dusted in powdered sugar, and cinnamon snickerdoodles with their characteristic crinkled top.

episodes.title: Soufflés
episodes.description: Martha tackles the notoriously temperamental soufflé, breaking down the technique into manageable steps. She prepares a bittersweet chocolate soufflé, a bright lemon version with raspberry coulis, and a classic savory cheese soufflé — proving the dish is less fragile than its reputation suggests.

episodes.title: French Pastry
episodes.description: The season finale tours classic French small pastries. Martha makes buttery croissants with their requisite honeycomb interior, golden shell-shaped madeleines scented with lemon zest, and financiers — the almond-brown butter cakes beloved by Parisian pastry shops.

episodes.title: Cookies
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on cookies, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Martha moves from the individual cookies of other episodes to an ambitious assortment spanning multiple techniques: drop, rolled, pressed, and sandwich. She demonstrates how different fat ratios produce different textures and how a baker can work efficiently to produce variety from a single session.

episodes.title: Coffee Cakes
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on coffee cakes, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Streusel-topped, ribbon-filled, and glazed — Martha explores the full range of coffee cake styles designed to accompany a morning cup. She explains what makes a coffee cake distinct from a layer cake and how to balance the crumb against a generous streusel.

episodes.title: Shortbread
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on shortbread, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Martha distills shortbread to its essence: butter, flour, and sugar in the right ratio, mixed as briefly as possible and baked at low heat. She makes classic Scottish rounds, chocolate-dipped fingers, and a lemon-glazed pan shortbread with a thick, sandy texture.

episodes.title: Custards
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on custards, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Egg-thickened desserts span the temperature spectrum — Martha makes a perfectly set crème caramel, a barely trembling baked egg custard, and a stovetop pastry cream used as the foundation of many French pastries.

episodes.title: Brioche
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on brioche, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. The rich, buttery French bread gets a full episode devoted to its unique properties. Martha makes a classic tête à tête, a large loaf, and a brioche tart base, explaining how the high butter content requires patience and cold fermentation.

episodes.title: Cakes
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on cakes, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Martha covers the fundamental cake categories — butter cakes, oil cakes, and genoise — and explains how each mixing method produces a distinct crumb. She makes a one-bowl cake, a classically creamed butter cake, and a genoise layered with jam and cream.

episodes.title: Basic Breads
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on basic breads, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. An approachable introduction to yeast bread: Martha shows how to judge dough development by feel, proof properly in a warm spot, and shape rolls and loaves without fear. She bakes a white sandwich loaf and whole-wheat dinner rolls.

episodes.title: Souffles
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on souffles, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Martha revisits the soufflé with additional detail: the base can be a béchamel, a pastry cream, or a fruit purée. She makes a Grand Marnier dessert soufflé and a sharp cheese soufflé, emphasizing that the technique is straightforward once practiced.

episodes.title: Croissants
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on croissants, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. The laminated croissant — layers of dough and cold butter folded repeatedly — is explained step by step. Martha makes classic plain croissants and filled ones with almond cream and chocolate, showing how the same dough produces different results.

episodes.title: Tarts
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on tarts, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Martha assembles several tarts using different shells and fillings: a classic fruit tart on pastry cream in a pâte sucrée shell, a rustic free-form galette, and a creamy tarte Tatin with caramelized apples and flaky pastry.

episodes.title: Special Breads
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on special breads, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Beyond white and whole wheat, Martha explores breads enriched with seeds, nuts, dried fruits, and spices. She makes a walnut-raisin country loaf, a seeded rye, and a holiday stolen with marzipan and candied peel.

episodes.title: Tuiles
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on tuiles, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. Tuiles — thin, crisp, curved cookies named for the French roof tiles they resemble — are a pastry shop staple. Martha shows how to spread the batter thinly, bake to the right color, and shape them over a rolling pin while still warm.

episodes.title: Focaccia and Pizza
episodes.description: Martha focuses the episode on focaccia and pizza, teaching the underlying technique that makes each version succeed. The Italian dimpled flatbread and its pizza cousin come from similar doughs but behave differently in the oven. Martha makes a rosemary-olive oil focaccia with a generous drizzle before baking and a Neapolitan-style pizza with a properly blistered crust.

episodes.title: Old-Fashioned Fruit Desserts
episodes.description: Classic American fruit desserts — the kinds that appear in church cookbooks and county fair competitions — get Martha's careful attention. She makes a proper peach cobbler, a deep-dish blueberry buckle, and a brown-butter-laced plum cake.

episodes.title: Breakfast
episodes.description: The morning pastry repertoire: Martha makes buttery morning buns with orange zest and cinnamon, a flaky biscuit, and a Dutch baby pancake that puffs dramatically in the oven.

episodes.title: Bar Cookies
episodes.description: Bar cookies offer the efficiency of a single pan and the richness of a full cookie assortment. Martha makes fudgy brownies, lemon bars with shortbread crust, and pecan squares with a caramel layer.

episodes.title: Puddings
episodes.description: Stovetop puddings and baked puddings make up this episode: a silky chocolate pudding thickened with cornstarch, a classic rice pudding simmered in cream, and a self-saucing chocolate lava pudding.

episodes.title: French Classics
episodes.description: Martha covers the foundational French pastry preparations that appear on every tasting menu: canelés with their lacquered crust and custardy interior, mille-feuille with stacked puff pastry and pastry cream, and classic Paris-Brest.

episodes.title: Pies
episodes.description: An episode dedicated entirely to the American pie canon. Martha makes a classic two-crust apple pie with a lattice top, a silky chocolate cream pie, and a lime curd meringue pie with the meringue browned to perfection.

episodes.title: Crackers and Flatbreads
episodes.description: Homemade crackers and flatbreads are simpler than most home bakers realize. Martha makes seeded crispbreads, whole-grain lavash, and a classic rosemary flatbread that can be broken at the table.

episodes.title: Cupcakes
episodes.description: Martha elevates the cupcake beyond its everyday incarnation: a lemon-curd-filled vanilla cupcake with cloud frosting, a devil's food cupcake with Swiss meringue buttercream, and a carrot cupcake with whipped cream cheese frosting.

episodes.title: Holiday Breads
episodes.description: Breads associated with specific holidays and celebrations across cultures: a Greek tsoureki for Easter, a brioche-based Christmas stollen, and a traditional king cake for Mardi Gras with its hidden fève.

episodes.title: Chocolate
episodes.description: A chocolate-focused episode spanning technique and format: tempering dark chocolate for bark and truffles, making a light chocolate chiffon cake, and baking dense chocolate cookies dusted in powdered sugar.

episodes.title: Bundt Cakes
episodes.description: The Bundt pan's decorative design requires no frosting — Martha shows how to use it to advantage with a marble swirl cake, a lemon-glazed Bundt that needs only a drizzle, and a sour cream chocolate Bundt.

episodes.title: Cookies
episodes.description: A second cookie episode covering the more refined end of the spectrum: piped spritz cookies pressed from a cookie gun, thin crisp florentines laced with candied orange and almonds, and Mexican wedding cookies rolled in powdered sugar.

episodes.title: Muffins
episodes.description: The humble muffin gets a serious treatment: Martha explains the quick bread method, the danger of over-mixing, and how to produce a high, domed muffin top. She makes corn muffins with jalapeño, bran muffins packed with raisins, and a classic blueberry.

episodes.title: Citrus
episodes.description: Lemon, lime, orange, grapefruit, blood orange, and Meyer lemon all make an appearance. Martha uses citrus in unexpected ways — caramelizing orange slices for tart garnish, using grapefruit zest in a glazed pound cake, and making a blood orange upside-down cake.

episodes.title: Northeast
episodes.description: New England and Mid-Atlantic baking traditions: cranberry walnut bread, maple-sweetened Boston cream pie with its characteristic chocolate glaze, and johnnycakes — the cornmeal pancakes of Rhode Island.

episodes.title: Pumpkin
episodes.description: Pumpkin earns a full episode as both vegetable and flavoring. Martha makes a silky pumpkin cheesecake, dense pumpkin bread with pepitas, and pumpkin-spice snickerdoodles that balance warmth and sweetness.

episodes.title: Nuts
episodes.description: Every nut gets a starring role: pecan praline crunch layered into a coffee cake, walnut rugelach with apricot jam, and a pistachio semolina cake redolent with rose water.

episodes.title: Caramel
episodes.description: The chemistry of caramel — dry versus wet method, the stages of sugar cooking — gets a thorough lesson. Martha makes salted caramel sauce, a caramel apple tart, and caramel-dipped shortbread with a crunchy coating.

episodes.title: Fruit Desserts
episodes.description: A Valentine's Day-adjacent episode using seasonal winter fruit — poached quinces in red wine, a raspberry-rose pavlova, and individual cherry clafoutis served in ramekins.

episodes.title: Phyllo
episodes.description: Paper-thin phyllo dough opens a world of possibilities. Martha makes baklava layered with honey and pistachios, a savory spanakopita with feta and spinach, and delicate phyllo cups filled with lemon cream.

episodes.title: Spiked
episodes.description: Alcohol as an ingredient in baking: rum-soaked rum cake, Guinness-enriched chocolate cake, and bourbon pecan pie. Martha explains how spirits add flavor, help with moisture retention, and can prevent crystallization in candies.

episodes.title: Southern
episodes.description: The baking traditions of the American South: a tall coconut layer cake with Italian meringue frosting, hummingbird cake with cream cheese frosting, and cakey red velvet with classic cream cheese icing.

episodes.title: Gluten-Free Baking
episodes.description: Martha explores naturally gluten-free flours and techniques. She bakes a dense flourless chocolate cake, almond-flour financiers, and a polenta pound cake scented with rosemary — proving that removing wheat doesn't mean removing pleasure.

episodes.title: Chocolate Techniques
episodes.description: A masterclass in chocolate technique: tempering dark chocolate to a glossy snap, making molten lava cakes with a properly liquid center, and a layered chocolate-hazelnut tart using three preparations of the same ingredient.

episodes.title: Honey
episodes.description: Martha showcases honey as a primary baking ingredient rather than a sweetener afterthought. She makes a Greek honey cake soaked in warm spiced honey, baklava with three types of nuts and floral honey, and honey-lavender madeleines.

episodes.title: Caramelized and Crisp
episodes.description: The season finale focuses on caramelization: a properly made tarte Tatin with deeply caramelized apples and buttery pastry, tuiles pressed into cylinders, and a financier variation that browns the butter to a hazelnut intensity.

episodes.title: Never Enough Chocolate
episodes.description: An all-chocolate episode covering the full spectrum: from a single-origin dark chocolate bar cake to milk chocolate truffles and white chocolate bark with dried cherries. Martha explains how cocoa percentage affects texture and flavor.

episodes.title: Danish
episodes.description: The Scandinavian laminated pastry gets a full demonstration of its multi-step process: the détrempe, the butter block, the folds and turns. Martha forms cheese Danish, fruit-filled envelopes, and braided Danish loaves.

episodes.title: Pulled Doughs
episodes.description: Babka and strudel share the characteristic of their doughs being stretched and pulled rather than rolled. Martha makes a chocolate-swirl babka and a classic apple strudel stretched paper-thin over a table.

episodes.title: Celebration Cakes
episodes.description: Cakes designed for marking milestones: a naked layer cake decorated with fresh flowers, a luxurious multi-tier fondant cake, and a dramatic black and white checkered interior cake that reveals its pattern when sliced.

episodes.title: Bake It Dark
episodes.description: Deep, dark flavors dominate: molasses gingerbread, a buckwheat honey cake, and a darkly caramelized tarte Tatin left on the heat just long enough to develop its characteristic amber color.

episodes.title: Coconut
episodes.description: Coconut in every form — shredded, toasted, desiccated, as flour, and as cream — appears across an episode of tropical-leaning desserts. Martha makes a layered coconut cake, coconut macaroons, and a coconut cream tart.

episodes.title: Coffee
episodes.description: Coffee as a baking ingredient gets its moment: espresso-soaked ladyfingers in a classic tiramisu, coffee buttercream on a vanilla layer cake, and coffee-cardamom shortbread cookies.

episodes.title: Green Tea
episodes.description: Matcha — Japanese stone-ground green tea — provides the distinctive flavor in a matcha Swiss roll with white chocolate cream, matcha-white chocolate madeleines, and green tea shortbread with sesame.

episodes.title: Extraordinary Fruits
episodes.description: Less-common fruits get the baking spotlight: a fig and almond tart, a persimmon pudding cake, and a passion fruit soufflé demonstrating the fruit's extraordinary acidity and perfume.

episodes.title: Pâte Feuilletée
episodes.description: Rough puff pastry — faster and slightly more forgiving than the classical version — gives Martha the material for a Napoleonic mille-feuille, a lattice-topped blueberry tart, and flaky hand pies filled with lemon curd and cream cheese.

episodes.title: Spiced
episodes.description: The holiday spice rack in full: a spiced rum bundt cake glazed with brown butter, a cardamom-scented Swedish tea ring, and cinnamon roll babka bridging two traditions.

episodes.title: Candy
episodes.description: Martha treats candy-making as a branch of baking, applying the same precision to sugar temperatures. She makes brittle with roasted peanuts, a toffee bark dipped in dark chocolate, and caramel-filled milk chocolate bonbons.

episodes.title: Boozy Baking
episodes.description: The holiday finale explores alcohol as a baking ingredient: a classic rum cake soaked after baking, a Champagne layer cake for New Year's, and bourbon-spiked eggnog bread pudding with a vanilla caramel sauce.

episodes.title: Fruit Curds
episodes.description: Lemon curd is Martha's gateway to the full family of citrus curds. She makes the classic lemon version, then applies the method to lime and passion fruit, using each as a tart filling, a cake filling, and a simple spread on scones.

episodes.title: Homemade Doughnuts
episodes.description: Martha fries doughnuts in three categories: yeast-raised glazed, old-fashioned buttermilk cake, and baked doughnut holes tossed in cinnamon sugar. She explains why proper oil temperature is the most critical variable.

episodes.title: Chocolate Ganache
episodes.description: The simplest and most versatile of chocolate preparations — equal parts chocolate and cream — becomes ganache, the building block of truffles, tarts, and frosting. Martha adjusts the ratios to produce a pourable glaze, a whipped filling, and a firm truffle center.

episodes.title: Sponge Cake
episodes.description: The sponge cake — light, airy, relying on whipped eggs rather than chemical leavening — forms the backbone of European pastry. Martha makes a classic génoise, an angel food cake, and a jelly roll sponge.

episodes.title: Frangipane
episodes.description: Frangipane — the almond cream spread on tart bases before fruit is arranged on top — appears in pear Bourdaloue tart, a raspberry frangipane galette, and almond-filled croissant dough formed into bear claws.

episodes.title: White Bread
episodes.description: The fundamental white sandwich loaf — soft, with a tender crust — gets a definitive recipe. Martha also makes white rolls for dinner service and an enriched white pullman loaf baked in a lidded pan for a perfectly square slice.

episodes.title: Never Enough Cookies
episodes.description: An ambitious cookie episode featuring seven varieties: thin-and-crisp chocolate chip, soft peanut butter, chewy oatmeal raisin, shortbread, chocolate crinkle, molasses, and elegant rosette spritz.

episodes.title: Pizza Dough
episodes.description: Pizza dough is a gateway to countless flatbreads. Martha makes a Neapolitan-style dough for a classic margherita, a whole-wheat version for a vegetable pizza, and a thick Sicilian-style dough for a pan pizza baked in olive oil.

episodes.title: One Bowl Desserts
episodes.description: Desserts that require no mixer and only a single bowl prove that great baking does not demand equipment. Martha makes a one-bowl chocolate cake, brownies stirred by hand, and a yogurt olive oil cake from the Mediterranean tradition.

episodes.title: Layered Yeast Dough
episodes.description: The Danish pastry family extends to croissant dough and kouign-amann — the Breton butter cake that caramelizes as it bakes. Martha makes all three from a similar laminated base.

episodes.title: Pastry Cream
episodes.description: Pastry cream — crème pâtissière — fills éclairs, Napoleons, and fruit tarts. Martha makes a classic version and variations: lightened with whipped cream for diplomat cream, and flavored with chocolate and praline.

episodes.title: French Meringue
episodes.description: The simplest of the three meringue types — raw egg whites whipped with sugar — forms the base for vacherin, baked Alaska, and tiny meringue kisses piped and dried overnight in a low oven.

episodes.title: Press-In Crusts
episodes.description: No rolling pin needed: Martha makes press-in crusts from graham cracker crumbs, ground nuts, and cookie crumbs that form perfectly consistent shells for cheesecakes, cream pies, and no-bake tarts.

episodes.title: Classic New England
episodes.description: New England's baking heritage: Indian pudding made with cornmeal and molasses, a Boston brown bread steamed in a can, and cranberry-walnut muffins that showcase the region's signature berry.

episodes.title: Mid-Atlantic
episodes.description: The mid-Atlantic states contribute shoofly pie from Pennsylvania and New York-style cheesecake. Martha makes both alongside a Maryland beaten biscuit using the traditional method.

episodes.title: Midwest
episodes.description: The Midwest's baking is defined by abundance and simplicity: a farm-style apple cake with brown sugar glaze, a church-supper layer cake, and German-influenced stollen from Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine neighborhood.

episodes.title: Northwest
episodes.description: The Pacific Northwest brings Dungeness crab to the table, but its baking tradition features huckleberries, hazelnuts, and Dungeness crabs aside — Martha focuses on hazelnut cake and huckleberry pie.

episodes.title: Southern Classics
episodes.description: The American South's baking tradition runs deep: red velvet cake, pecan pie, and a proper Lane cake — the Alabama specialty layered with a bourbon-raisin-pecan filling.

episodes.title: New England
episodes.description: A deeper dive into New England baking: anadama bread with cornmeal and molasses, a maple-glazed apple cake, and hermit bars — the spice cookies that kept well for Yankee sea voyages.

episodes.title: Gulf
episodes.description: Gulf Coast baking reflects its French, Spanish, and African heritage: a king cake in carnival colors, beignets dusted with powdered sugar, and a praline-pecan sweet potato pie.

episodes.title: Pennsylvania Dutch
episodes.description: The Pennsylvania Dutch tradition produces fastnachts (fried doughnuts for Fat Tuesday), wet-bottom shoofly pie, and funnel cake.

episodes.title: South Atlantic
episodes.description: Georgia and the Carolinas: a hummingbird cake with pineapple and banana, sweet tea pound cake, and benne seed wafers from the African culinary tradition.

episodes.title: West
episodes.description: California and the West Coast's baking scene reflects its multicultural heritage: sourdough bread from San Francisco, a Persian love cake with rose water, and avocado chocolate mousse cake.

episodes.title: Southwest
episodes.description: The Southwest brings chile heat and blue corn to baking: a blue corn cornbread, bizcochitos (the official cookie of New Mexico), and a chocolate-chile tart.

episodes.title: South
episodes.description: A Christmas Eve episode celebrating Southern baking at Christmas: Divinity candy, ambrosia cake, and a traditional Lady Baltimore cake with dried fruits and nuts.

episodes.title: Great Lakes
episodes.description: New Year's Eve explores the Great Lakes baking tradition: Finnish nisu (cardamom bread), Michigan cherry pie, and a Polish chrusciki (angel wings) for the New Year.

episodes.title: Updated Classics
episodes.description: Martha revisits beloved classics and gives each a contemporary update: a brown butter chocolate chip cookie, a citrus-flecked lemon poppy seed loaf, and a black sesame layer cake that reinterprets the classic vanilla birthday cake.

episodes.title: Coffee Shop Favorites
episodes.description: The pastry case of a great coffee shop: vanilla bean scones with a proper crust, morning glory muffins packed with carrot and pineapple, and a flaky croissant-style kouign-amann.

episodes.title: For the Cookie Jar
episodes.description: A cookie jar should always hold these: Martha makes the ideal chocolate chip, a proper oatmeal raisin, and a thick peanut butter cookie with a fork crosshatch pressed in the center.

episodes.title: Alternative Crusts
episodes.description: Pie crusts that go beyond butter and flour: a cream cheese crust for fruit tarts, a lard crust for a pork pot pie (Martha's grandmother's preference), and a pressed almond-meal tart shell.

episodes.title: Flour Power
episodes.description: Different flours produce dramatically different results. Martha bakes with almond flour, spelt, einkorn, and rice flour — showing how each behaves and what flavors it brings to cookies, cakes, and breads.

episodes.title: Seeded
episodes.description: Seeds — sesame, poppy, sunflower, caraway, fennel — transform breads and pastries. Martha makes a seeded rye bread, poppy seed roll, and tahini shortbread.

episodes.title: Yeasted Breakfast Favorites
episodes.description: Breakfast yeasted pastries beyond croissants: Martha makes cinnamon rolls with cream cheese icing, sticky buns with pecan caramel, and a braided Swedish cardamom bread.

episodes.title: Better (For You) Bake Sale
episodes.description: Whole-grain, less-sugar bake sale items that still taste worth buying: oat-date energy bars, whole-wheat banana bread, and dark chocolate-almond clusters with coconut sugar.

episodes.title: Bakery-Style Cookies
episodes.description: The large, thick, bakery-counter cookie that holds its shape and texture for days: giant M&M cookies, thick-cut snickerdoodles, and oversized triple-chocolate cookies.

episodes.title: Naturally Gluten-Free
episodes.description: Desserts that happen to contain no gluten: a flourless chocolate cake, a polenta olive oil cake with rosemary, and coconut macaroons dipped in chocolate.

episodes.title: Breads and Rolls
episodes.description: A bread episode covering three staples: a rustic country sourdough with open crumb, potato dinner rolls that stay soft for days, and a pretzel roll with a lye-like baking soda wash.

episodes.title: Rethinking Cake
episodes.description: Cakes that challenge convention: a savory tomato upside-down cake served as appetizer, an olive oil cake perfumed with Calabrian orange, and a bean-based black bean chocolate cake.

episodes.title: Wholesome Breakfast
episodes.description: The new year begins with a wholesome breakfast menu: whole-grain waffles with fruit compote, egg white omelets baked in the oven, and a smoothie bowl with granola baked from scratch.

episodes.title: Scandinavia
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Scandinavia, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Pepparkakor from Sweden, Finnish gingerbread, and Norwegian krumkake pressed in a decorative iron represent Scandinavia's spiced, crisp cookie tradition.

episodes.title: Australia and New Zealand
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Australia and New Zealand, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Anzac biscuits — the oat and golden syrup cookies named for World War I soldiers — lead an Antipodean cookie episode alongside New Zealand afghan biscuits and Australian Tim Tams.

episodes.title: North America
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from North America, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Classic North American cookies that everyone recognizes: the Toll House chocolate chip, the snickerdoodle, and the New York black and white cookie.

episodes.title: Austria, Germany, Switzerland
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Austria, Germany, Switzerland, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. The German-speaking world's holiday cookie tradition: Zimtsterne (cinnamon star cookies), Springerle pressed with carved molds, and Swiss mailänderli butter cookies.

episodes.title: Latin America
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Latin America, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Alfajores from Argentina — dulce de leche sandwiched between cornstarch shortbread — polvorones from Mexico, and Brazilian pão de mel honey spice cookies.

episodes.title: Eastern Europe
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Eastern Europe, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Rugelach from the Ashkenazi tradition, Hungarian linzer cookies with apricot jam, and Polish chrusciki fried angel wings.

episodes.title: Italian Cookies
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Italian Cookies, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Biscotti with pistachios and dried cranberries, ricciarelli (almond paste Sienese cookies), and pizzelle pressed in a decorative iron.

episodes.title: Cookies of Great Britain
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Great Britain, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Digestive biscuits, shortbread fingers, and Iced Gems — the tiny piped royal icing cookies on a base biscuit that are a British childhood staple.

episodes.title: Middle Eastern Cookies
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Middle Eastern Cookies, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Ma'amoul (date-filled semolina cookies pressed in carved molds), baklava bites, and Lebanese ghraybeh butter cookies.

episodes.title: Cookies of Greece
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Greece, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Kourabiedes (butter almond cookies rolled in powdered sugar), melomakarona (honey walnut Christmas cookies), and finikia with syrup and sesame.

episodes.title: Cookies of the Netherlands
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from the Netherlands, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. Stroopwafels (thin waffle cookies sandwiched with caramel syrup), speculaas pressed in carved molds, and Dutch butter letters piped at Sinterklaas.

episodes.title: Classic Italian Cookies
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from Classic Italian Cookies, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. A second Italian episode focusing on classic pastry shop cookies: cantucci (twice-baked almond biscotti), savoiardi (ladyfingers), and brutti ma buoni ('ugly but good' hazelnut meringue drops).

episodes.title: French Cookies
episodes.description: Martha bakes cookies from French Cookies, exploring the regional techniques and traditional ingredients that define the style. The finale explores French cookie tradition: palmiers (puff pastry twists), Breton galettes (buttery shortbread), and tuiles à l'orange (thin crisp wafers shaped while warm).

episodes.title: Adorned Cakes
episodes.description: Martha covers the full vocabulary of cake decoration: fondant ruffles, sugar flowers, painted ganache panels, and piped royal icing lace.

episodes.title: Perfect Pâte à Choux
episodes.description: Choux dough gets its masterclass: éclairs with pastry cream and chocolate glaze, Paris-Brest with praline cream, and a croquembouche tower built from cream puffs and spun caramel.

episodes.title: Decorative Breads
episodes.description: Bread as sculpture: Martha braids a six-strand challah, shapes a wheat sheaf from dough, and scores a country loaf with an elaborate leaf pattern.

episodes.title: Elegant Cookies
episodes.description: Cookies that belong on a dessert plate rather than a cookie jar: painted shortbread, chocolate-dipped cigarettes, and florentines with a caramel-nut back.

episodes.title: Magnificent Meringues
episodes.description: Meringue sculpted into everything from simple kisses to elaborate Swiss meringue mushrooms for a bûche de Noël. Martha makes a pavlova wreath and individual vacherin cups.

episodes.title: Breakfast Pastries
episodes.description: Morning pastries that look as impressive as they taste: croissants with a perfect honey-comb interior, morning buns rolled in orange sugar, and iced cinnamon rolls piped with cream cheese frosting.

episodes.title: Fanciful Tarts
episodes.description: Tarts as expressions of the season: a summer fruit tart with a mosaic of strawberries and kiwi, a fall tart with caramelized figs and walnuts, and a stunning geode tart with isomalt sugar crystals.

episodes.title: Impressive Chocolate Desserts
episodes.description: Chocolate showstoppers: a mirror-glaze chocolate entremet, chocolate bark with tempered patterns, and a dramatic fallen soufflé cake served warm.

episodes.title: Decorated Cupcakes
episodes.description: Cupcakes elevated through decoration: a flower garden cupcake with petals piped in buttercream, an ombre cupcake with a gradient swirl, and a tiny landscape cupcake with fondant figures.

episodes.title: Perfect Puff Pastry
episodes.description: All-butter puff pastry made from scratch, then used for mille-feuille, palmiers, and a showpiece vol-au-vent for entertaining.

episodes.title: Embellished Pies
episodes.description: Pie decoration beyond the standard lattice: a braided crust edge, cutout leaf appliqués on top, and a woven geometric lattice for a mincemeat pie.

episodes.title: Frosted Cakes
episodes.description: Frosting as the star: how to achieve a perfectly smooth buttercream exterior, a sculpted rosette border, and the increasingly popular textured raked effect on layer cakes.

episodes.title: Patterned
episodes.description: Pattern in baking's final frontier: a checkerboard interior cake, a jelly roll with a spiral design, and a marble cake with deliberate swirls rather than random mixing.

episodes.title: Dried Fruit
episodes.description: Martha spotlights dried fruit as a baking powerhouse, adding concentrated sweetness and chewy texture. She bakes a rum-soaked fruitcake with golden raisins and apricots, date-walnut bars, and a cranberry-orange quick bread.

episodes.title: Apples
episodes.description: An episode dedicated to apples in baking, covering how variety choice changes texture. Martha makes a French apple tart with fanned slices on pastry cream, a chunky Appalachian stack cake, and warm apple fritters.

episodes.title: Cultured Dairy
episodes.description: Martha explores how sour cream, crème fraîche, buttermilk, and yogurt add tenderness and tang to baked goods. She makes a buttermilk bundt, crème fraîche cheesecake, and Greek yogurt pancakes.

episodes.title: Lemons
episodes.description: A celebration of lemon's brightness in baking. Martha prepares her signature lemon bars with shortbread crust, a lemon-ricotta cake with candied peel, and lemon curd-filled doughnuts dusted in powdered sugar.

episodes.title: Ginger
episodes.description: Ginger in three forms — fresh, ground, and crystallized — anchors the episode. Martha bakes a gingerbread layer cake with cream cheese frosting, crispy ginger snaps, and a fresh ginger cake with pear compote.
recipes: Fresh Ginger Cake with Pear Compote

episodes.title: Stone Fruits
episodes.description: Martha bakes with cherries, peaches, plums, and apricots at their summer peak. A sour cherry clafoutis, a peach upside-down cake, and apricot jam-filled hand pies show how stone fruit moves between rustic and refined.

episodes.title: Cocoa
episodes.description: Martha distinguishes between cocoa powder types and shows how each behaves differently in the oven. She makes a Dutch-process dark chocolate layer cake, a natural cocoa brownie with a fudgy center, and cocoa-dusted truffles.

episodes.title: Grapes
episodes.description: An unusual ingredient in baking, grapes prove their worth in a Tuscan schiacciata all'uva focaccia with Concord grapes, a grape and almond frangipane tart, and a roasted grape crostata.

episodes.title: Almonds
episodes.description: Almonds in every form — whole, sliced, ground into flour, and as paste — drive this episode. Martha bakes a flourless almond cake, classic Spanish tarta de Santiago, almond croissants, and chewy amaretti cookies.

episodes.title: Pantry Milks
episodes.description: Martha bakes with condensed milk, evaporated milk, and coconut milk, showing how each lends a distinctive sweetness and texture. She makes Vietnamese condensed milk crème caramel, coconut layer cake, and tres leches.

episodes.title: Berries
episodes.description: A summer berries episode covering strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries. Martha makes a classic strawberry shortcake, blueberry buckle with streusel topping, and individual raspberry-blackberry cobblers.

episodes.title: Citrus Zest
episodes.description: Martha demonstrates using citrus zest — lemon, lime, orange, grapefruit — as a primary flavoring agent in baking, going beyond juice to extract essential oils. She makes a five-citrus loaf, zested shortbread, and a creamy citrus tart.

episodes.title: Warm Spices
episodes.description: The spice rack's warming elements — cinnamon, cloves, star anise, allspice, cardamom — are woven into a spiced layer cake, mulled wine-poached pears in pastry, and a chai-spiced shortbread.

episodes.title: Stocks and Soups
episodes.description: The foundation of French cooking gets a full breakdown. Martha clarifies the difference between stock and broth, makes a rich chicken stock by carefully skimming fat and impurities, then uses it for classic French onion soup and a bright chicken noodle.

episodes.title: Eggs
episodes.description: Martha covers the egg's versatility across cooking techniques: perfect soft- and hard-boiled, French-style scrambled, a silky frittata, and a classic béarnaise sauce that teaches emulsification on the stovetop.

episodes.title: Chicken
episodes.description: A comprehensive chicken episode: Martha breaks down a whole bird, roasts one using the high-heat method, pan-sears boneless thighs to crispy-skinned perfection, and makes a quick pan sauce demonstrating fond deglazing.

episodes.title: Fish and Shellfish
episodes.description: Martha explains how the delicate proteins in fish and shellfish demand quick, confident cooking. She pan-sears salmon skin-side-down for crisp skin, steams mussels in white wine and shallots, and poaches halibut in court bouillon.

episodes.title: Vegetables
episodes.description: Martha covers blanching, roasting, and sautéing vegetables to bring out their best qualities. She blanches haricots verts to a vibrant green, roasts root vegetables with honey and thyme, and makes a quick stir-fry of seasonal greens.

episodes.title: Beef and Lamb
episodes.description: Martha teaches the difference between tender and tough cuts and the cooking method each demands. She braises short ribs low and slow, roasts a rack of lamb with an herb crust, and quick-cooks strip steak with compound butter.

episodes.title: Pasta
episodes.description: Martha rolls and cuts fresh egg pasta by hand, dresses fettuccine in a proper Bolognese that simmers for hours, and tosses pappardelle with a simple brown butter and sage sauce that comes together in minutes.
recipes: Pappardelle with Brown Butter and Sage

episodes.title: Sauces
episodes.description: The five French mother sauces organized around technique. Martha makes a velvety béchamel, a rich velouté, and hollandaise — explaining how each becomes a template for dozens of derivative sauces used in both home and restaurant cooking.

episodes.title: Grains
episodes.description: Grains beyond rice get a showcase. Martha makes a saffron risotto using the proper add-stock-slowly method, cooks farro as a warm salad with roasted vegetables, and prepares classic polenta finished with Parmesan and butter.

episodes.title: Breads
episodes.description: Martha bakes a no-knead rustic country loaf with a crackly crust, whole-wheat sandwich bread shaped into a proper Pullman loaf, and quick skillet cornbread that can accompany dinner on a weeknight.

episodes.title: Desserts
episodes.description: Martha applies culinary school logic to dessert: a properly tempered chocolate mousse built on pâte à bombe, a classic crème brûlée torched to an even amber crust, and a vanilla bean panna cotta that sets to the perfect jiggle.

episodes.title: Salads
episodes.description: Martha reframes the salad as a technique-driven course. She makes a classic Caesar dressing from scratch with anchovy and raw egg, a warm duck confit salad with frisée, and a composed Niçoise with tuna, haricots verts, and olives.
recipes: Warm Duck Confit and Frisée Salad

episodes.title: Entertaining
episodes.description: Martha applies all the skills from the season to create a dinner party menu. She prepares cheese gougères to pass with cocktails, a butterflied leg of lamb, and ratatouille made from the season's best vegetables.

episodes.title: Perfect Roast
episodes.description: Martha applies culinary school logic to the roast: resting meat before carving, using a thermometer rather than guessing by time, and making a jus from the pan drippings. She roasts both a chicken and a leg of lamb.

episodes.title: Stewing
episodes.description: Low-and-slow wet cooking unlocks tough cuts. Martha makes a classic beef bourguignon, explains how to maintain a bare simmer (not a boil), and shows how to adjust seasoning at the end of a long braise.

episodes.title: Soups
episodes.description: Three soup techniques: a clear consommé clarified with a raft, a creamy purée of leek and potato, and a hearty minestrone that works as a meal.

episodes.title: Vegetables
episodes.description: Vegetables as the main course: Martha makes a vegetable tian with overlapping slices of zucchini and tomato, glazed carrots in butter and stock, and a whole roasted cauliflower.

episodes.title: Pasta
episodes.description: Pasta beyond boiling: Martha makes pasta from scratch, cooks a proper carbonara (no cream), and demonstrates a cacio e pepe that relies entirely on starchy pasta water for its sauce.

episodes.title: Pasta Sauces
episodes.description: The foundational Italian pasta sauces: a slow-cooked Bolognese, a quick amatriciana, and a classic pesto from the Ligurian tradition.

episodes.title: Pasta Sauces Part 2
episodes.description: The second pasta sauce episode covers cream-based preparations: an Alfredo made properly with butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano (no cream), a Gorgonzola cream sauce for gnocchi, and a classic ragù bianco.

episodes.title: Sautéing
episodes.description: The French technique of quick cooking in hot fat: Martha explains the difference between sautéing and pan-frying, makes sole meunière in browned butter, and sautés chicken breasts to a golden, juicy finish.

episodes.title: Dumplings
episodes.description: Dumplings from three traditions: Chinese jiaozi folded and pan-fried (potstickers), Italian gnocchi made from potato dough, and German Käsespätzle pressed through a colander.

episodes.title: Grains
episodes.description: Beyond rice: Martha cooks farro as a warm salad, makes a creamy polenta, and prepares a millet pilaf — showing how each grain responds differently to liquid ratios and cooking time.

episodes.title: Preserving
episodes.description: The science and art of preservation: Martha makes strawberry jam with precise pectin ratios, quick pickled vegetables in vinegar brine, and lacto-fermented sauerkraut.

episodes.title: Legumes
episodes.description: From dried beans to fresh peas: Martha makes a proper cassoulet with confit duck and sausage, a hummus from scratch with dried chickpeas, and a lentil soup with cumin-tempered oil.

episodes.title: Shrimp
episodes.description: Shrimp in all its forms: quickly sautéed with garlic and white wine, butterflied and grilled with herb butter, and in a classic Louisianan shrimp étouffée.

episodes.title: Chicken
episodes.description: Martha returns to chicken — the most versatile of proteins — with new techniques: a spatchcocked bird cooked quickly at high heat, a braised thigh with olives and capers, and a chicken saltimbocca wrapped in prosciutto.

episodes.title: Onions
episodes.description: The onion family gets a complete episode: slow-caramelized onions for a tart, pickled red onions for tacos, and a soubise sauce — the classic French onion cream — for serving with roasted meats.

episodes.title: Roasting
episodes.description: The dry heat method for developing flavor: Martha explains the Maillard reaction, shows how to roast a beet properly (in foil, not wet), and makes a complete roasted rack of pork with fennel.

episodes.title: Noodles
episodes.description: Noodles from Asia to Europe: Martha makes Japanese soba cold with dipping sauce, Vietnamese pho from a proper bone broth, and a Taiwanese scallion noodle with chili oil.

episodes.title: Braising
episodes.description: Braising — submerging meat partially in liquid and cooking covered at low heat — is a transformative technique. Martha braises lamb shanks in red wine until falling from the bone and makes short ribs with a gremolata finish.

episodes.title: Rice
episodes.description: Rice cooked three ways: absorption method for Persian saffron rice (with the crispy tahdig crust), risotto style with constant stirring and stock addition, and steamed rice in a bamboo basket.

episodes.title: Know Your Vegetables
episodes.description: A vegetable identification and technique episode: Martha covers which vegetables to store in the refrigerator versus room temperature, how to break down kohlrabi and celery root, and which vegetables are better steamed versus roasted.

episodes.title: Grains
episodes.description: A second grains episode covering ancient grains: freekeh roasted in a pilaf, amaranth as a hot breakfast cereal, and teff in an Ethiopian-style injera flatbread.

episodes.title: Sauces
episodes.description: Sauce-making beyond the mother sauces: Martha makes a chimichurri for grilled meats, a classic French beurre blanc with white wine and butter, and a romesco — the Catalan nut and pepper sauce.

episodes.title: Pork
episodes.description: Pork's full range: a cured and smoked pork belly made at home, a quick pork scaloppine with lemon and capers, and a whole shoulder slow-roasted until pull-apart tender.

episodes.title: Potatoes
episodes.description: Everything the potato can do: a proper gratin dauphinois with cream and Gruyère, pommes Anna built from thinly sliced discs of potato crisped in butter, and a twice-baked potato stuffed with sharp cheddar.

episodes.title: Salads
episodes.description: Composed salads as a main course: Martha makes a grain salad with toasted farro, a Cobb salad with blue cheese dressing, and a classic salade Lyonnaise with lardons and a warm vinaigrette.

episodes.title: Corn
episodes.description: Corn at its seasonal best: a Mexican-style elote (grilled corn with chili, lime, and cotija), a summer corn chowder, and a Southern spoonbread baked in a cast iron skillet.

episodes.title: Eat Your Greens
episodes.description: Leafy greens get technique-forward treatment: Martha wilts spinach properly (leaving no water to dilute the pan), braises escarole with anchovies and white beans, and makes a kale Caesar with homemade croutons.

episodes.title: One-Pot Meals
episodes.description: The efficiency of one-pot cooking: Martha makes a chicken and rice in a Dutch oven, a pasta e fagioli in a single pot, and a Moroccan chicken tagine with preserved lemons.

episodes.title: Steakhouse
episodes.description: The steakhouse experience recreated at home: a dry-aged-style ribeye cooked in cast iron with herb butter, a classic wedge salad with blue cheese dressing, and a creamy horseradish sauce.

episodes.title: Mushrooms
episodes.description: Mushrooms deserve their own episode: Martha sautés mixed mushrooms with thyme and cream for a pasta sauce, makes a mushroom risotto with porcini stock, and prepares stuffed portobello mushrooms.

episodes.title: Sandwiches
episodes.description: Martha elevates the sandwich: a proper cubano pressed and griddled, a croque madame with béchamel and egg, and a bánh mì with house-pickled daikon and carrots.

episodes.title: Turkey
episodes.description: Turkey beyond Thanksgiving: Martha dry-brines a whole turkey breast for faster weeknight roasting, makes turkey meatballs in a classic Italian Sunday sauce, and a turkey scaloppine.

episodes.title: French Bistro Classics
episodes.description: The French bistro menu: steak frites with proper café de Paris butter, moules marinières with crusty bread, and a crème caramel unmolded at the table.

episodes.title: The Grind
episodes.description: Grinding meat at home: Martha grinds chuck for a superior burger, lamb and pine nuts for a Middle Eastern kefta, and pork with sage for breakfast sausage patties.

episodes.title: Cooking with Wine
episodes.description: Wine's role in cooking: Martha makes a wine-braised chicken coq au vin, risotto with a full bottle of Barolo, and a zabaglione beaten to a froth over a bain-marie.

episodes.title: Italian Favorites
episodes.description: Italian comfort food: a veal ossobuco braised with gremolata, a classic eggplant parmigiana layered without frying, and a properly set panna cotta.

episodes.title: On the Bone
episodes.description: Cooking meat on the bone delivers superior flavor — Martha demonstrates with a bone-in prime rib, lamb chops grilled on the bone, and braised oxtail in red wine.

episodes.title: Cheese
episodes.description: Cooking with cheese beyond melting it on pizza: Martha makes a fromage fort (blended cheese spread), a soufflé au Comté, and gougères.

episodes.title: Lamb
episodes.description: A comprehensive lamb episode: a Moroccan spiced leg with chermoula, a quick lamb kebab, and lamb chops with a pistachio crust.

episodes.title: Arabian Gulf Breakfast
episodes.description: Season 5 explores Arabian Gulf cuisine. Martha opens with breakfast staples: balaleet (vermicelli with egg and cardamom), chebab (saffron pancakes with date syrup), and a thick laban drink.

episodes.title: Grilled Favorites
episodes.description: Gulf grilling tradition: whole fish marinated in chermoula and grilled over coals, shish tawook (chicken skewers with garlic and yogurt), and a grilled vegetable medley.

episodes.title: Stews of the Arabian Gulf
episodes.description: Gulf stews — harees (slow-cooked wheat and lamb) and margoog (meat and vegetable stew with thin bread) — demonstrate the region's hearty, slow-cooked tradition.

episodes.title: Breads
episodes.description: Gulf breads: khameer (saffron-scented leavened rounds), rigag (crispy thin crepe-like bread), and a fluffy khobz oven bread.

episodes.title: Side Dishes
episodes.description: Essential Gulf accompaniments: a spiced lentil dish, muhammar (sweet saffron rice), and a roasted carrot salad with cumin and yogurt.

episodes.title: Entertaining for a Crowd
episodes.description: A Gulf-themed feast for many guests: slow-roasted ouzi (whole lamb), saffron rice with nuts and raisins, and mezze spreads.

episodes.title: Dates
episodes.description: The date palm's fruit in its many applications: stuffed Medjool dates with almond paste, a date and walnut cake, and date molasses drizzled over labneh.

episodes.title: Kebabs
episodes.description: Kebabs of the Gulf region: kafta kebab of spiced ground meat, a fish kebab with turmeric and coriander, and a vegetable kebab with halloumi.

episodes.title: Festive Occasions
episodes.description: Gulf celebration cooking: machboos (spiced rice with meat), a whole roasted chicken with Gulf baharat blend, and luqaimat (sweet fried dumplings) in date syrup.

episodes.title: Small Bites
episodes.description: Gulf meze and small plates: samboosa (crispy triangular pastries), filled with spiced lamb, shrimp spring rolls, and fattoush salad.

episodes.title: Coastal Favorites
episodes.description: Gulf coastal cooking with fresh catch: a whole baked fish in salt crust, sautéed prawns with vermicelli, and a shrimp biryani.

episodes.title: Sweets
episodes.description: Arabian sweets: umm ali (bread pudding with cream and pistachios), muhallabia (milk pudding with rose water), and baklava in the Gulf style with cardamom.

episodes.title: Cooking with Grains
episodes.description: Gulf grain traditions: jareesh (cracked wheat porridge with meat), freekeh with roasted vegetables, and a sesame-studded brown rice.

episodes.title: Azaleas and Tree Peonies
episodes.description: Actor Jesse Tyler Ferguson visits Martha's farm during peak azalea bloom, and the two walk the grounds cataloging colors and varieties. Martha explains her decades-long project of building a collection of tree peonies and azaleas that create a spectacular spring show.

guests.name: Jesse Tyler Ferguson
guests.context: Actor known for Modern Family; avid gardener himself

episodes.title: Flower Power
episodes.description: An episode devoted to cutting flowers from Martha's extensive garden for arrangements throughout the house. She demonstrates how to cut at the right time of day, condition stems, and arrange blooms in her characteristically natural, abundant style.

episodes.title: Martha Vegs Out
episodes.description: The season finale harvests the vegetable garden at peak summer abundance. Martha and Ryan work through tomatoes, zucchini, beans, and herbs, then Martha heads into the kitchen to prepare a complete summer meal from what they brought in, closing the loop from seed to table.

guests.name: Ryan McCallister
guests.context: Martha's gardener; worked the harvest alongside her

episodes.title: Pasta Night
episodes.description: Martha launches her Roku cooking series with a pasta-focused episode that feels like watching a master class in a home kitchen. She makes fresh pappardelle by hand and tosses it in a slow-cooked lamb ragù, then prepares a quick weeknight linguine with clams.

episodes.title: Roast Chicken
episodes.description: Martha returns to the dish she believes reveals a cook's true competence: the perfect roast chicken. She explains her high-heat method, the importance of trussing, and how to rest the bird. Pan drippings become the base for an herb-lemon pan sauce.

episodes.title: Holiday Cookies
episodes.description: A seasonal episode showcasing Martha's most beloved holiday cookie recipes. She decorates rolled sugar cookies with royal icing, makes spiced pfeffernüsse, and bakes buttery spritz cookies using her vintage cookie press.

episodes.title: Seafood Feast
episodes.description: Martha showcases the range of her seafood cooking: a whole roasted branzino with herbs and olives, seared scallops finished with brown butter and capers, and a classic shrimp cocktail with housemade horseradish sauce.

episodes.title: Winter Soups
episodes.description: Three hearty soups for cold months. Martha makes a French onion soup with a properly bubbling Gruyère crown, a silky butternut squash purée brightened with ginger, and a rustic white bean and escarole soup built on good chicken stock.

episodes.title: Steak Night
episodes.description: Martha demystifies cooking steak at home, explaining how to read the cut, season aggressively with salt well in advance, and achieve a perfect crust in a cast-iron skillet. A bone-in ribeye and a lean flank steak with chimichurri show the technique's range.

episodes.title: Salads for All Seasons
episodes.description: Martha argues that the best salads require technique, not just assembly. She massages kale with lemon and olive oil for a sturdy winter salad, builds a proper Niçoise for summer entertaining, and makes a warm roasted beet salad with goat cheese and walnuts.
recipes: Roasted Beet and Goat Cheese Salad

episodes.title: Brunch at Home
episodes.description: Martha makes the case for hosting brunch at home instead of going out. She prepares eggs Benedict with a foolproof blender hollandaise, ricotta pancakes topped with fresh berries, and a batch of bloody marys using her garden's tomatoes.

episodes.title: Vegetable Sides
episodes.description: An episode focused entirely on making vegetables the star of the table. Martha roasts cauliflower until caramelized, braises fennel in white wine until silky, and makes a spectacular gratin dauphinois layered with Yukon Gold potatoes and cream.

episodes.title: Classic Desserts
episodes.description: Martha's final episode of Season 1 revisits her most essential desserts: a proper tarte Tatin with golden, caramelized apples inverted onto flaky pastry, a dark chocolate pot de crème, and her legendary rice pudding with vanilla and cream.

episodes.title: Perfect Chicken Dinner
episodes.description: Martha revisits the perfect chicken dinner from multiple angles — a spatchcocked bird roasted on a bed of vegetables, a braised whole chicken in white wine and tarragon, and crispy pan-seared thighs dressed with a quick pan sauce. The episode demonstrates why chicken remains the most instructive protein in any cook's repertoire.

guests.name: Kevin Sharkey
guests.context: Martha's longtime creative director; joined for the dinner segment

episodes.title: Maine Lobster Dinner
episodes.description: Maine lobster in its many forms: a classic boiled whole lobster with drawn butter, a chilled lobster salad in a butter-toasted roll, and a creamy lobster bisque that uses every part of the shell for maximum flavor.

episodes.title: Pizza Perfection
episodes.description: Martha explores two iconic pizza traditions with expert help. A Sicilian pizza gets its airy, thick crust from a high-hydration dough proofed in an oiled pan, while a Neapolitan pie demands a screaming-hot oven and minimal toppings.

guests.name: Christian Petroni
guests.context: Pizza chef; demonstrated Neapolitan technique

guests.name: Dean Medico
guests.context: Pizza chef; demonstrated Sicilian-style pizza

episodes.title: Japanese Cuisine
episodes.description: Martha explores the precision and artistry of Japanese cooking: hand-formed nigiri sushi with seasoned rice, sashimi cut to proper thickness, and miso soup built on a careful dashi.

episodes.title: Brunch Favorites
episodes.description: Martha's definitive brunch menu, updated for a new decade: Dutch baby pancakes puffed high in a cast-iron skillet, avocado toast elevated with poached eggs and everything-bagel spice, and a citrus-forward French 75 cocktail.

episodes.title: Croissants and Sourdough
episodes.description: The two most technically demanding breads get dedicated treatment. Martha laminate croissant dough through multiple folds over two days, and guides viewers through maintaining and baking with a sourdough starter.

episodes.title: One Pot Wonders
episodes.description: The efficiency of one-pot cooking gets an upgrade: a beef and vegetable stew cooked entirely in a Dutch oven, a Spanish-style chicken and rice where everything melds together, and a one-pan salmon with roasted vegetables.

guests.name: Jamie Oliver
guests.context: British celebrity chef; joined Martha for a one-pot collaboration

episodes.title: Martha Throws a Tea Party
episodes.description: An Edwardian institution revived: Martha sets a proper afternoon tea with finger sandwiches, scones served with clotted cream and lemon curd, and a tier of petit fours and miniature cakes.

episodes.title: Martha and the Chocolate Factory
episodes.description: A chocolate-lover's episode: Martha tempers chocolate for bark and truffles, makes a flourless chocolate torte that's part fudge, part ganache, and demonstrates the proper way to make hot chocolate from scratch using single-origin cacao.

episodes.title: Perfect Burger Three Ways
episodes.description: Three distinct burgers: a classic smash burger with American cheese on a potato bun, a lamb burger with tzatziki and cucumber, and a turkey burger with avocado that proves the category doesn't require beef.

episodes.title: Today's Catch: Fish Recipes for Everyday
episodes.description: Martha makes a case for cooking fish at home more often with three achievable weeknight preparations: a whole branzino roasted with fennel and white wine, pan-seared halibut with brown butter and capers, and a quick Thai-style fish curry.

episodes.title: India: A Tour of Food
episodes.description: Martha explores the breadth of Indian cuisine by cooking from different regional traditions: a Mughal-style chicken korma fragrant with cardamom, a South Indian coconut fish curry, and a whole-wheat paratha from the tandoor tradition.

episodes.title: Magic Mushrooms
episodes.description: An episode celebrating fungi in all their forms: a deeply savory mushroom risotto with truffle oil, crispy roasted king oyster mushrooms served as a meat substitute, and a simple mushroom toast on sourdough with herbs.

episodes.title: Picture Perfect Rolled Lasagna
episodes.description: Martha rolls individual portions of fresh pasta around a ricotta and spinach filling, creating lasagna rolls that are both impressive and practical for entertaining. A slow-cooked tomato sauce and béchamel layer over the top.

episodes.title: Easy Homemade Dumplings
episodes.description: Martha demystifies dumpling-making: pan-fried pork and cabbage gyoza with a crispy bottom, steamed shrimp har gow in a translucent wrapper, and boiled soup dumplings with a gingery broth inside.

episodes.title: The Bagel Show
episodes.description: Martha bakes proper New York-style bagels from scratch — boiled in a malt-water bath before baking — then builds a complete smoked salmon spread with all the traditional accompaniments.

episodes.title: Martha's Favorite Cakes
episodes.description: Three cakes that Martha has returned to throughout her career: her mother's lemon chiffon with a cloud of whipped cream, a properly fudgy devil's food with ganache frosting, and a carrot cake with the right balance of spice and cream cheese icing.

episodes.title: Vegan Cuisine Redefined
episodes.description: Martha approaches plant-based cooking with her usual precision: a cashew-cream pasta that mimics the richness of dairy, roasted cauliflower steaks with a harissa glaze, and a coconut milk-based panna cotta that sets just as perfectly as the dairy version.

episodes.title: Authentic Greek Cuisine
episodes.description: Martha explores the sunny, herb-forward flavors of Greek cooking: a proper spanakopita with hand-layered phyllo, grilled lamb chops with tzatziki and horiatiki salad, and loukoumades — hot Greek honey doughnuts — for dessert.

episodes.title: Jean-Georges and the Tin Building
episodes.description: Martha visits legendary chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten's Tin Building food hall in New York, exploring his approach to market-driven cooking. The episode captures the breadth of his culinary philosophy from street food to fine dining.

guests.name: Jean-Georges Vongerichten
guests.context: Three-Michelin-starred chef; creator of the Tin Building food hall

episodes.title: Martha Hosts a Derby Party
episodes.description: Kentucky Derby season inspires an elegant outdoor entertaining spread: mint juleps in silver cups, a bourbon-glazed smoked ham, and a showstopper Derby pie with chocolate and pecans. Martha explains the hospitality rituals that make Derby parties distinctly American.

episodes.title: The Art of Raw Food
episodes.description: Crudo, tartare, and ceviche: Martha demonstrates the art of serving raw and barely-touched proteins with confidence. She makes a tuna crudo with yuzu and olive oil, a beef tartare with classic condiments, and a citrus-cured salmon tiradito.

episodes.title: Baking Baguettes and Breads
episodes.description: Martha tackles the baguette — the bread many home bakers fear most — explaining the hydration, the scoring, and the steam injection that produces a crackly crust. She also makes a pain de campagne and a whole-grain einkorn loaf.

episodes.title: Chef David Burke's Modern Classics
episodes.description: Celebrity chef David Burke joins Martha to demonstrate his distinctive approach to American cooking: a pastrami salmon with everything-spice crust, a cheesecake lollipop for dessert, and his signature pretzel-crusted crab cake.

guests.name: David Burke
guests.context: Celebrity chef known for modern American cuisine and creative presentations

episodes.title: All Things Yogurt
episodes.description: Yogurt as an ingredient across sweet and savory applications: a tangy yogurt-marinated roast chicken, a cucumber-yogurt soup served chilled, a thick labneh with olive oil and za'atar for dipping, and a yogurt panna cotta with berry compote.

episodes.title: Sensational Summer Salads
episodes.description: Four salads that justify themselves as a complete meal: a fattoush with crispy pita and sumac, a grilled peach and burrata salad, a warm farro salad with roasted beets and goat cheese, and a refreshing watermelon-mint-feta combination.

episodes.title: Martha Throws a Clam Bake
episodes.description: A proper New England clam bake assembled on a sheet pan for home cooks. Martha layers clams, mussels, corn, potatoes, and andouille sausage, steaming everything together in the oven. The episode captures the communal spirit of coastal summer eating.

episodes.title: Rustic Italian Cuisine
episodes.description: Three dishes from Italy's farmhouse tradition: a ribollita — the Tuscan bread soup that improves with reheating — bistecca alla Fiorentina cooked over fierce heat, and a panna cotta with aged balsamic.

episodes.title: Exploring Korean Cuisine
episodes.description: Martha steps into Korean cooking with three preparations: a proper bibimbap with seasoned vegetables and fried egg, japchae — glass noodles stir-fried with vegetables and beef — and a simple doenjang-jjigae fermented soybean paste soup.

episodes.title: Martha's Favorite Brunch
episodes.description: The season finale revisits brunch with Martha's all-time favorites: shakshuka with tomatoes and feta, a proper croque-madame with béchamel and a runny egg, and a citrus-dressed fruit salad that serves as both opener and closer.

episodes.title: Ice Cream Show
episodes.description: Martha explores ice cream in all its forms with artisan ice cream maker Ben Van Leeuwen. They make a classic French custard base, a dairy-free coconut ice cream with mango swirl, and a savory gorgonzola-walnut ice cream that pairs with salad.

guests.name: Ben Van Leeuwen
guests.context: Founder of Van Leeuwen Ice Cream; collaborated on artisan flavors

episodes.title: Japanese Knife Skills
episodes.description: Chef Masa Takayama — one of the world's premier Japanese chefs — joins Martha to demonstrate the philosophy and technique behind Japanese knife work. They break down a whole fish Japanese-style and prepare sashimi with surgical precision.

guests.name: Masa Takayama
guests.context: Chef-owner of Masa NYC, three-Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant

episodes.title: Mexican Cuisine
episodes.description: Chef Lazaro Perez guides Martha through regional Mexican cooking that goes beyond tacos: a mole negro from Oaxaca built on dozens of dried chiles and chocolate, carnitas braised in lard until shreddable, and a tres leches soaked in three milks.

guests.name: Lazaro Perez
guests.context: Mexican chef specializing in regional and traditional preparations

episodes.title: Arethusa Farm Dairy
episodes.description: Martha visits Arethusa Farm, Connecticut's celebrated dairy operation, to explore award-winning artisan cheese production. The episode follows milk from the cows to the aging cave and concludes with Martha cooking with the farm's cheeses.

episodes.title: Brioche, Tarts and Pie
episodes.description: Martha collaborates with Chef Margarita Lorenzana-Manzke on enriched doughs and pastry. They make a cloud-soft brioche loaf, a Basque cheesecake baked until burnished on the outside and custard within, and an open-faced summer berry tart.

guests.name: Margarita Lorenzana-Manzke
guests.context: Chef and pastry expert; co-owner of Bicyclette Bistro in Los Angeles

episodes.title: Tomato Show
episodes.description: At the height of summer tomato season, Martha devotes an entire episode to the fruit: a slow-roasted tomato confit that can be stored in oil, a classic Caprese with heirloom varieties and aged balsamic, and a savory tomato tarte Tatin.

episodes.title: French Bistro Night
episodes.description: Martha recreates a classic French bistro dinner at home: steak frites with proper shoestring fries and a Dijon-cream sauce, a silky onion tart, and profiteroles filled with vanilla ice cream and draped in hot chocolate sauce.

episodes.title: The Science of Woks and Frying
episodes.description: Chef Kenji Lopez-Alt — food science authority — joins Martha to explain the physics of wok cooking and deep frying. They make beef and broccoli with proper wok hei, tempura vegetables with the correct batter consistency, and Japanese karaage chicken.

guests.name: Kenji Lopez-Alt
guests.context: Chef, author of The Food Lab; food science expert

episodes.title: Perfect Weekend Breakfast
episodes.description: Martha's definitive weekend morning spread, assembled with care: a leek and gruyère frittata that comes to the table in its cast-iron skillet, homemade granola with toasted coconut, and a proper hollandaise spooned over asparagus.

guests.name: Laura Kim
guests.context: Fashion designer; joined Martha for a leisurely weekend breakfast conversation

episodes.title: Jacques Pepin Cooking His Way
episodes.description: Martha welcomes Jacques Pépin — her peer and one of France's greatest cooking ambassadors in America — for a warm, collegial episode. They make omelettes together (comparing their slightly different techniques), a fast French lentil salad, and Pépin's beloved chocolate mousse.

guests.name: Jacques Pépin
guests.context: Legendary French-American chef, author, and TV host; longtime friend of Martha

episodes.title: Premiere
episodes.description: Martha Stewart hosts the premiere of her own Apprentice spin-off, introducing 16 candidates competing for a top position at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia. The task: design a floral arrangement and table setting for a high-profile event. Martha's boardroom style — precise, demanding, but instructive — establishes the show's tone immediately.

guests.name: Jim Bozzini
guests.context: Contestant; fired in the premiere episode

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Martha's daughter; served as boardroom aide throughout the series

episodes.title: Retail
episodes.description: The candidates manage a retail selling challenge at a Martha Stewart Living store, competing on sales technique and product knowledge. Martha evaluates which candidates understand her brand and which are merely performing.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Martha's daughter; boardroom aide

episodes.title: Magazine
episodes.description: Two teams compete to create a magazine spread that would fit the Martha Stewart Living aesthetic. Martha evaluates layouts, photography, and editorial voice, singling out candidates who understand how lifestyle media works.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Catering
episodes.description: The candidates cater a high-end party, planning the menu and service. Martha tests whether they can maintain the standard of quality that carries her name — both in food preparation and in presentation.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Flowers
episodes.description: A floral design challenge tasks the teams with creating arrangements for a corporate event. Martha — an expert flower arranger — evaluates the results with the kind of precision that made her famous.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Renovation
episodes.description: The teams renovate a room in a specified time period, applying Martha's principles of design, color, and functionality. Martha evaluates not just the outcome but the process — how they made decisions under pressure.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Fabric
episodes.description: A textile and fabric challenge draws on the manufacturing side of Martha's business. The candidates design a home textile product and pitch it for potential inclusion in the Martha Stewart line.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Baking
episodes.description: The candidates bake and sell product — testing both their kitchen skills and their retail ability. Martha observes who can produce at a commercial level while maintaining quality standards.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Housewares
episodes.description: A housewares design challenge requires candidates to conceptualize and pitch a new product for the Martha Stewart home collection. Martha evaluates originality, practicality, and brand alignment.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Farming
episodes.description: The candidates visit a farm and work through agricultural tasks — testing whether they can embrace the hands-in-the-dirt side of the Martha Stewart brand as well as the elegant entertaining side.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Holiday
episodes.description: A holiday entertaining challenge tests whether the candidates understand the Martha Stewart holiday aesthetic — how to balance tradition with fresh ideas and achieve the kind of effortless elegance Martha is known for.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Decorating
episodes.description: An interior decorating challenge puts Martha's design principles to the test. The candidates decorate a space on a budget, demonstrating resourcefulness while meeting Martha's exacting standards for color, texture, and proportion.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Cooking School
episodes.description: The candidates teach a cooking class — demonstrating whether they can share Martha's knowledge effectively with an audience. Martha evaluates their teaching ability alongside their technical cooking skills.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Garden Party
episodes.description: A garden party challenge tests the candidates' ability to orchestrate an elegant outdoor event, from the floral centerpieces to the food to the guest experience. Martha evaluates the event as a whole entity.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide

episodes.title: Final Task
episodes.description: The two finalists each organize a major event — a complete Martha Stewart-style celebration — with former candidates as their teams. Martha and her advisors assess every detail before making the final decision.

guests.name: Alexis Stewart
guests.context: Boardroom aide and evaluator

guests.name: Charles Koppelman
guests.context: MSLO board member; evaluator

guests.name: Sharon Patrick
guests.context: MSLO president; evaluator

episodes.description: The season finale: Martha chooses her Apprentice in the boardroom. Dawna Stone is named the winner and offered a role at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia. guests.name: Marcia Cross

episodes.description: An early Season 1 episode features Donald and Melania Trump joining Martha in the kitchen to make meatloaf — a contrast of glamour and domesticity that became one of the show's talked-about moments.

episodes.title: George Foreman Visits
episodes.description: Boxing legend and grill entrepreneur George Foreman visits Martha's kitchen for a conversation about entrepreneurship and cooking. Martha demonstrates her technique for making perfect burgers while Foreman talks about his famous grill and family.

guests.context: Boxing champion and entrepreneur behind the George Foreman Grill
